title: How a pressure cooker cooks food faster
examples: Why does a pressure cooker cook faster?
How hot does a pressure cooker get?
Why does a pressure cooker whistle?

explain.say: In an open pan, water can never get hotter than about 100 degrees, because at that point it boils away as steam. That limits how fast food cooks.

draw.text: How a pressure cooker cooks food faster

explain.say: A pressure cooker has a lid that locks and seals. As the water heats, steam is trapped, and the pressure inside climbs.
Higher pressure makes it harder for water to turn into steam, so its boiling point rises. At about double normal air pressure, water boils at about 120 degrees.
Hotter water cooks food much faster, often in a third of the time. A weighted valve lets steam escape if the pressure gets too high, which makes the hiss or whistle.

faq.q: Why does a pressure cooker cook faster?
faq.a: Trapped steam raises the pressure, which raises the boiling point of water to about 120 degrees. Food cooks much faster at that higher temperature.
asks: How does a pressure cooker work?

faq.q: How hot does a pressure cooker get?
faq.a: At full pressure, about one bar above normal air pressure, the water inside reaches about 120 degrees instead of 100.
asks: What temperature does water boil at in a pressure cooker?

faq.q: Why does a pressure cooker whistle?
faq.a: The whistle or hiss is steam escaping through the pressure valve. It opens when the pressure reaches the set level, keeping it steady and safe.
asks: What is the weight on top of a pressure cooker?

faq.a: Modern ones have several safety features: a valve that releases extra steam, a backup safety valve or plug, and a lid that cannot be opened while under pressure.

faq.q: Why does water boil at a lower temperature on mountains?
faq.a: It is the opposite of a pressure cooker: lower air pressure high up lets water boil below 100 degrees, so food cooks more slowly. Mountaineers use pressure cookers for this reason.
asks: Why is it hard to cook on a mountain?

facts: At about 2 bar absolute pressure, double normal air pressure, water boils at about 120 °C.
Denis Papin demonstrated a steam digester, an early pressure cooker, in 1679.
